subject: Request: Deferred invoicing cadence + Net-90 approval for Stratus Health
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@stratushealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@stratushealth.com
Date: Thu, May 28, 2026 at 08:34 AM -0700
Subject: Request for quarterly invoicing + Net-90 payment terms

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood and we think the platform will solve a lot of our latency/cost issues for inference. Procurement has one ask before we can proceed: Stratus runs on a quarterly fiscal cycle and our treasury team requires a single invoice per quarter rather than monthly billing, and they prefer Net-90 payment terms from invoice date.

Attached is a draft PO for Q3 that shows the expected spend cadence. Can your billing team confirm whether Redwood can support a quarterly invoice schedule with Net-90? If Net-90 is not possible, is Net-60 an option? We are targeting a FastTrack start on July 1 pending billing confirmation.

Appreciate any flexibility here — Stratus is committing to a 12-month reserved capacity package if we can align on terms.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Procurement, Stratus Health

Karthik/Marissa — looping you in. Customer (Stratus Health) is asking for quarterly invoicing + Net-90. They are prepared to sign a 12-month reserved capacity (high priority).

Key asks:
- Quarterly invoice (one invoice per quarter covering the committed reserved spend)
- Net-90 from invoice date (or Net-60 fallback)

Marissa, can you add details on the revenue uplift and discount request they mentioned verbally? Karthik, we need deal desk and finance to confirm whether we can agree to Net-90 and any required conditions (e.g., credit check, early-payment fees, security deposit).

I attached the customer's PO for reference.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, May 28, 2026 at 11:05 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for quarterly invoicing + Net-90 payment terms

Team — pulling together the commercial ask. Quick summary:
- ARR impact: ~$1.1M ARR over 12 months (reserved capacity plan).
- Requested billing: Quarterly invoices, Net-90. Customer indicated constrained treasury timing; this is a strategic account in healthcare.
- Trade-offs suggested by customer: preference for a small upfront commitment and quarterly invoices in exchange for a 5% list price concession.

From a sales perspective, this is a strong logo and good reference value in US healthcare. I recommend approval with these guardrails:
1) Require a signed Master Services Agreement with the proposed terms and a DocuSign envelope for contract + SOW.
2) Add a clause for an annual review and 60-day notice for changes in billing cadence.
3) Security deposit or ACH pre-authorization as a condition for Net-90 (finance to confirm).

Marissa, can you confirm the margin hit at 5%? Rishi — requesting your sign-off or escalation to finance for Net-90 approval.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachment: proposed-terms-Redwood-Stratus.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, May 28, 2026 at 14:43 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for quarterly invoicing + Net-90 payment terms

Thanks for the context. A few items I need before I can approve Net-90:
- Precedent: Do we have recent customers in healthcare with Net-90? If so, send examples and whether we required deposits.
- Risk assessment: quick summary of revenue-at-risk and creditworthiness (attach any credit check).
- Controls: proposed contract language for late payments, interest, and recovery steps.

Michael — can you run a quick credit check and advise on whether a security deposit or progressive billing (first invoice 50% upfront, then quarterly thereafter) is more appropriate? If finance is comfortable, I can approve Net-90 for this strategic account with the conditions above.

Rishi
VP, Commercial Operations
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, May 29, 2026 at 17:21 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for quarterly invoicing + Net-90 payment terms

Team — completed review and recommendation: see attached customer-risk-summary.pdf. Summary: Stratus Health has clean payment history with two vendors using Net-60 but not Net-90 historically. Treasury is credible but will need standard KYC and a signed ACH authorization.

Approval decision (Finance):
- Approve quarterly invoicing.
- Approve Net-60 standard; Net-90 can be approved conditionally for the first two quarters only if the customer provides: (a) an executed ACH authorization or wire guarantee, OR (b) a security deposit equal to one quarter's committed spend.
- Require a clause in the MSA for interest on late payments (1.5% monthly) and termination rights after 60 days past due.

Next steps for sales:
1) Update the SOW and MSA to include the above conditions and route to DocuSign (HubSpot deal updated).
2) Ask customer to complete ACH authorization or confirm ability to provide deposit.
3) Finance will re-evaluate after two quarters for any permanent Net-90 approval.

I'll initiate the DocuSign envelope once legal confirms the MSA language.

-Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
